title: Planning-node lookup lives in the template module
description:
Move the pure lookup that finds a container's bracket planning node, and the container-label interpolation it depends on, out of `commands` into `crate::templates`, so the validation layer stops importing it from `commands`.

## Background

- `find_planning_node` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:2280-2305`), `PLAN_DOC_LABEL` (`:2319`) and `planning_node_plan_path` (`:2328-2334`) are pure functions over issues and a `GraphTemplate`. `commands/mod.rs:96` re-exports the two functions for `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:682-683`, an inverted dependency from the validation layer onto `commands`.
- `find_planning_node` calls `declared_container_label` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template_expand.rs:626-653`, `pub(super)`), which interpolates container tokens through `InterpolationContext` (`template_expand.rs:528-610`). Template application also uses both (`commands/template.rs:14-15,916`; the `template_expand.rs` tests at `:1221-1303`).
- `crate::templates` (`crates/jit/src/templates.rs`) already owns `GraphTemplate` (`:279`), `RoleBindings` (`:226`) and `GraphTemplate::plan_doc_location` (`:511`), and imports nothing from `commands`.
- Callers: `commands/validate.rs:967-968` (`plan_document_paths`), `:1042-1043` (`plan_content_with_issues`), `validation/repository.rs:682-683` (`project_plan_content`), `commands/template.rs:916`, and the unit test `test_find_planning_node_resolves_template_declared_container_label` (`commands/validate.rs:2537`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `find_planning_node`, `planning_node_plan_path`, the plan-document label and `declared_container_label`, with the container-token interpolation they use, are defined under `crate::templates`; `commands` defines and re-exports none of them.
- [hard] REQ-02: `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs` resolves planning nodes through `crate::templates`, and no production code under `crates/jit/src/validation/` names a `crate::commands` item for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Template application and validation resolve the same planning node and container label as before: the moved unit test passes in the templates module, and the template-application and scope-validation suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Planning-node and container-label resolution move from commands into crate::templates.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure lookup moves between modules with its import sites and one test.

title: One resolver for plan-document references
description:
Resolve a breakable container's plan document in one function and make every site that needs it call that function.

## Background

The chain breakable type → container template with a plan-document location → planning node → planning node's `plan`-labelled document reference is written three times:

- `plan_document_paths` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:949-972`) derives the paths a validation capture must read;
- `plan_content_with_issues` (`commands/validate.rs:1008-1055`) reads the content for graph-rule evaluation, and serves mutation callers too (`commands/mod.rs:2685,3175`, `commands/dependency.rs:403`, `commands/bulk_update.rs:377`, and `commands/issue.rs:90` through `plan_content_from_image`);
- `project_plan_content` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:657-695`) reads the content inside repository validation.

The two content readers share one rule: an absent plan whose planning node is not `done` is omitted, and an absent plan whose planning node is `done` is an error. The scope-validation tests over external plans (`crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/scope_validation_tests.rs:909-1085,1196,1221`) exercise the rule end to end.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One pure function in `crate::templates` maps a container, the issues by id and the template registry to the container's plan-document reference, or none, together with whether its planning node is `done`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `plan_document_paths`, `plan_content_with_issues` and `project_plan_content` obtain plan-document references only through that function; no other code walks from a breakable type to a planning node's plan document.
- [hard] REQ-03: One templates unit test owns the resolution cases: an inline plan (no reference), a relinked non-default path, and the not-done and done planning node; the scope-validation suite passes unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Capture discovery, plan-content projection and repository validation resolve plan documents through one function.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three copies of one resolution collapse into one pure function in one focused change.

title: Configuration accessors for content format and strictness
description:
Give `JitConfig` one accessor for the repository's default content format and one for its validation strictness, each applying the default when `[validation]` or the key is absent, and move the validation layer and projection rendering onto them.

## Background

- `[validation].content_format` and `[validation].strictness` are typed at load: absent means Markdown and loose respectively (`crates/jit/src/config.rs`, `ValidationConfig`).
- Callers restate the default when `config.validation` is `None`. In the validation layer and repository state: `collect_rule_findings` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:561-566`), `collect_item_link_findings` (`validation/repository.rs:707-712`), and `repo_content_format` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/projection_render.rs:245-260`, called at `:102`), which also re-implements the token match with its own error.

- [hard] REQ-02: The three listed readers read the content format through `JitConfig::content_format()`, and `projection_render.rs` keeps no token matching or default of its own.
- [hard] REQ-03: Config unit tests show both accessors' result for an absent `[validation]` table, an absent key and a declared value.

title: Local rules compile each schema once per evaluation set
description:
Compile the local rules' JSON Schemas once and reuse them across issues, so whole-repository validation stops recompiling every schema for every issue.

## Background

- `evaluate_local` (`crates/jit/src/validation/local.rs`) desugars each matching rule's schema (`:302-305`) and builds a new `SchemaEngine` per call (`:316-317`). The engine caches compiled validators by schema key (`crates/jit/src/validation/engine.rs:177-183,408-440`), but the cache lives only for that one call.
- Repository validation calls `evaluate_local` once per issue (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:568-576`), so each schema compiles once per issue.
- Single-issue write paths also call `evaluate_local` (`commands/mod.rs`, `commands/template.rs`, `commands/bulk_update.rs`, `commands/gate_check.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`) and its tests (`validation/local.rs`, `repository_state/default_rules.rs`, `tests/fast_docs_templates/content_format_dispatch.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/example_rulesets_tests.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/default_rules_registry_derivation_tests.rs`). `SchemaEngine` is `!Sync`, which suits a single-threaded report.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A compiled local-rule set holds the desugared schemas and one `SchemaEngine`, and evaluates any number of issues; each distinct schema compiles at most once per set.
- [hard] REQ-02: `evaluate_local` keeps its signature and builds a compiled set for its one issue, so its callers are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Repository validation evaluates every issue through one compiled set per validation.
- [hard] REQ-04: A unit test evaluates two issues against one compiled set and shows that both use the same compiled validator for a shared schema.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Graph findings record their firing subject
description:
Record on every graph finding the issue whose rule application fired it, so a selection can tell the firing subject apart from the issue the finding is attributed to.

## Background

Constructors: `for_issue` (`:277`), `unattributed` (`:289`), `issue_finding` (`:742`) and `config_error` (`:753`); `evaluate_one` (`:600-690`) dispatches the assertion kinds.
- Attribution and subject differ in two cases: a `label-coverage` finding with `container-from-label` is attributed to the resolved container while the breakdown issue fired it (`:960-1060`), and a pointer that resolves to no issue or to several is a configuration error with no attribution although one issue fired it (`resolve_container` call sites in the same range).

- [hard] REQ-02: Graph unit tests show a `container-from-label` coverage finding attributed to the container with the breakdown issue as subject, an unresolvable pointer reported as a configuration error whose subject is the firing issue, and a `label-uniqueness` finding with no subject.
- [hard] REQ-03: Attribution, messages and severities are unchanged, and the existing graph and validation suites pass unchanged.

title: Container pointers resolve through an index built once per graph evaluation
description:
Resolve `container-from-label` pointers against an issue-id index built once per graph evaluation, removing the per-pointer scan that dominates validation time.

## Background

- `resolve_container` (`crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:1306-1316`) parses the pointer as an `IssueIdPrefix` and tests it against every issue with `IssueIdPrefix::matches`, which normalises (allocates a lowercase, hyphen-free copy of) each candidate id. It runs once per pointer label, from `evaluate_label_coverage` (`:960-1060`) and `graph_rule_plan_source_ids` (`:501-525`), so resolution is O(labels × issues) allocations.
- A release-build profile of `jit validate` on this repository attributes about 29% of inclusive time to that normalisation (`dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/investigation.md`, capture part, C4).
- The prefix type lives in `domain::identity`. Unique, ambiguous and unresolved outcomes are asserted by the graph tests at `graph.rs:2702,2768,2877`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each graph evaluation builds one index over its resolution issues, and every container pointer resolves through it without normalising candidate ids.
- [hard] REQ-02: Unique, ambiguous and unresolved pointers resolve exactly as before, the minimum prefix length included; the existing graph tests pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A graph unit test resolves pointers given in different case and hyphenation against one index and shows the unique, ambiguous and unresolved outcomes.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Graph evaluation resolves container-from-label pointers through one id index instead of normalising candidate ids per pointer.

title: One loader parses the index and issue records
description:
Parse `.jit/index.json` and every indexed issue record through one loader, and make repository validation, validation capture and mutation bases call it.

## Background

Three loaders parse the same records:

- `load_records` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:353-415`) parses the index with `RepositoryIndex::parse`, every indexed record in index order, checks each record's embedded id, and reconciles the captured `.jit/issues` listing against the index.
- `effective_index_ids` and `effective_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:773-802`) parse the index through a private `IndexIds` struct and the records leniently, over overlay-effective bytes during capture.
- `captured_active_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2062-2100`) parses both through `storage::json::parse_repository_index`, reports a missing record as issue-not-found and returns the issues sorted by id (`:2093`); mutation bases, gate checking, archive and gate commands call it.

Kept as one change for a build reason: the three private loaders are replaced together, and an uncalled private function fails the zero-warning build.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One function in `repository_state` parses the index and every indexed record from a byte source into parsed records (index ids and issues in index order), checking embedded ids and, where the listing was captured, reconciling it against the index; its errors are typed.
- [hard] REQ-02: `load_records`, `effective_index_ids`, `effective_issues`, the `IndexIds` struct and `captured_active_issues`' own parsing no longer exist; each former caller calls the loader.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each caller keeps its contract: mutation captures still return issues sorted by id and report a missing indexed record as issue-not-found, and repository validation keeps index order and reports index, record and listing disagreements with today's messages.
- [hard] REQ-04: Unit tests own the loader's cases: a well-formed set, a missing record, a mismatched embedded id, an unparseable record and a listing that disagrees with the index.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: The index and issue records are parsed by one loader shared by validation, capture and mutation bases.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three private loaders converge on one new loader; deleting them makes the change one unit.

- Callers: `commands/validate.rs` (`validate_silent` `:107-125`, `validate_repository_report` `:523-532`, `validate_repository_report_with_divergences` `:535-545`, `capture_validation_report` `:547-586`, `capture_repair_plan` `:650-703`), `commands/gate_check.rs` (`repository_rule_report` `:440-448`, `gate_findings_from_report` `:639-665`, the repository checker at `:1050-1055`), `commands/init.rs:284-292,498-520,680`, `commands/profile.rs:24,356,1427`, `commands/config.rs:328`, `main.rs` (the whole-repository branch of the `Commands::Validate` arm, which calls `validate_repository_report_with_divergences`), the tests in `validation/repository.rs` and `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/undeclared_taxonomy_tests.rs:183`.

title: One mutation and one post-fix report for validate --fix
description:
Make `jit validate --fix` derive every fix from one captured validation, publish them in one mutation, and always render the one report computed over the fixed repository.

## Background

- `validate_with_fix` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:42-97`) first runs a full validation whose result fix mode discards (`:44`), then publishes each hierarchy type fix (`detect_and_fix_hierarchy_issues` `:1140-1216`, `apply_type_fix` `:1218-1234`, reading the hierarchy and issue list from disk), the transitive reduction (`reduce_all_dependencies`, already one mutation), each readiness correction in up to ten passes (`check_pending_transitions` `:2081-2137`, one lifecycle mutation per correction through `auto_transition_to_ready` and `auto_transition_to_backlog`, `commands/issue.rs:817,834`) and the derived-state repair (`repair_derived_state` (`commands/validate.rs:599-643`), one mutation). It re-validates only when it applied a fix, so a zero-fix run over an index that disagrees with the issue files prints "No fixes needed" and exits 0 while plain `jit validate` fails.
- `auto_transition_to_backlog` has no other caller; `auto_transition_to_ready` is also called at `commands/issue.rs:873`.
- Pure derivations exist: `generate_fixes` over `detect_validation_issues` (`domain::type_taxonomy`), `derive_dependency_repair` (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:854`, private), `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` (`domain/types.rs`), and `derive_materialization` for derived state. `finalize` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:719`) turns issue intents into a plan, and `RepositoryDelta::new` (`repository_state/image.rs:1239-1256`) accepts concatenated actions and refuses duplicate targets.
- `test_apply_type_fix_preserves_concurrent_type_correction` (`commands/validate.rs:2874`) shows that a type correction saved between capture and apply survives.
- The `--fix` branch of the `Commands::Validate` arm in `main.rs`, which calls `validate_with_fix`, renders `{valid, fixes_applied, dry_run, message}` in JSON. `jit recover` calls `repair_derived_state` (`commands/claim.rs:733`) and keeps doing so.

Kept as one change for a build reason: the fix return value and its renderer compile only together.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `--fix` computes no report before deriving its fixes. It derives the hierarchy, reduction, readiness and derived-state fixes from one validation capture, folding the issue edits per issue, and publishes them all through one mutation; `--dry-run` derives the same plan and publishes nothing; when the captured records do not parse, no fix is derived and the post-fix report carries the structural failure.
- [hard] REQ-02: Readiness corrections apply `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` to the projected issue set until none remains, and no other readiness derivation is introduced; `detect_and_fix_hierarchy_issues`, `apply_type_fix`, `check_pending_transitions` and `auto_transition_to_backlog` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: `--fix` always computes one report over the repository as the fixes leave it, including when it applied none, and renders it as plain `jit validate` does, with the fix count and messages; its exit status follows that report. A harness test shows one publication carrying fixes of every class, and a CLI test over an index that disagrees with the issue files shows `--fix` failing as plain `validate` does, which fails on today's code.
- [hard] REQ-04: A harness test replaces `test_apply_type_fix_preserves_concurrent_type_correction`: a type correction saved between capture and publish survives the composed fix, which re-derives over the new state. The listed fix suites pass with their assertions on repository state unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour and output change: `--fix --json` carries the post-fix report fields and its exit status follows that report.
- A later pure readiness derivation that every mutation shares will replace the fixpoint loop in this change.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: --fix derives its fixes from one capture, commits them in one mutation and always shows one post-fix report.
